input: s is an ASCII lowercase string of length n. x,y are nonnegative safe-integer rewards for removing adjacent ab and ba respectively; require floor(n/2)*max(x,y) safe. Collections are ordinary finite dense arrays/lists, not subclasses, proxies, sparse/accessor-backed collections. Strings are ordinary/primitive strings. Every collection length and computed allocation size fits [0,4294967295], with padded sizes explicitly included. No concurrent mutation or built-in monkey-patching is allowed. Preconditions are not runtime-checked, and allocation/resource capacity or completion is not guaranteed by declared bounds. JavaScript integer inputs are primitive safe-integer Number, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt.
return: Maximum reward from any sequence of those adjacent-pair removals.
mutation_aliasing: Inputs and caller-held aliases remain unchanged; working state is private. The Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: Each removal consumes two characters and the declared bound covers every subtotal/combined score. Non-a/b letters remain barriers. Removing the higher-reward orientation first preserves an optimal count of later lower-reward pairs. All integer inputs/intermediates remain within [-9007199254740991,9007199254740991]; no bitwise coercion is used.
complexity: O(n+1) time/O(n+1) auxiliary space, including copied characters, retained first-pass stack, second-pass stack and returned pair wrappers. Each pass pushes/pops each character at most once. Bounds include ordinary built-in operations/allocations and assume bounded-word arithmetic, constant-time indexing, amortized append/pop and any explicitly stated hash/sort behavior.
